recipes.title: Healthyish Ferrero Rocher Pie

photos.alt: A slice of Ferrero Rocher pie lifted out of the tin
The pie with a slice cut out, showing the layers
A slice of Ferrero Rocher pie on a plate
Lifting a slice out, seen from above

wide.alt: A slice being lifted out of the whole Ferrero Rocher pie

recipes.intro: A fudgy date and hazelnut base, a silky chocolate mousse layer and a crunchy hazelnut top. The secret to that mousse? Silken tofu. No bake, no cream, just 7 ingredients.

groups.name: Filling
items: ⅔ cup dark choc chips, melted

groups.name: Topping
items: ⅓ cup dark choc chips, melted

method: Blitz the dates, hazelnuts and almond flour, then add the cocoa and blitz again.
Press the mixture into your tin.
Blend the tofu, the ⅔ cup of melted chocolate and ½ jar of hazelnut butter until silky.
Spread over the base and smooth it over.
Mix the rest of the melted chocolate with ¼ jar of hazelnut butter and spread it on top.
Sprinkle with chopped hazelnuts and chill until set.
recipes.tip: You'd never guess the mousse is made with silken tofu. Blend it until it's completely smooth for the silkiest filling.
recipes.seoTitle: Healthyish Ferrero Rocher Pie (No Bake, Made with Tofu)
recipes.description: A no-bake, healthyish Ferrero Rocher pie with a date and hazelnut base and a silky chocolate mousse made with silken tofu. 7 ingredients, 8g protein a slice.

recipes.title: I Tried 6 Healthy Chocolate Mousse Recipes
recipes.seoTitle: 6 Healthy Chocolate Mousse Recipes, Ranked: Silken Tofu vs Greek Yogurt vs Cottage Cheese
recipes.description: I tested 6 high-protein chocolate mousses: cottage cheese, Greek yogurt and silken tofu, each with dates or melted chocolate. Here's the ranking and all 6 recipes.
recipes.intro: I tried 6 healthy chocolate mousse recipes so you don't have to. Three high-protein bases (cottage cheese, Greek yogurt and silken tofu), each made two ways: with dates and cocoa, or with melted dark chocolate. Then I ranked them on taste, texture and protein.
tested: Add the sweetener to each base: dates and cocoa, or melted dark chocolate and cocoa.
Chill overnight, then taste them side by side.
summary: something I'd actually have for dessert
recipes.method: Blend until silky smooth, then chill.
recipes.tip: Want the most protein for your calories? Cottage cheese + dates wins on macros, with 5.8g of protein per 100 kcal. For pure dessert vibes, go silken tofu + chocolate.

photos.alt: Six bowls of chocolate mousse with cottage cheese, Greek yogurt and silken tofu
The three bases with dates, cocoa and melted chocolate before blending

recipes.title: Biscoff Banana Bread Pudding

photos.alt: A spoonful of Biscoff banana bread pudding lifted from the jar
The Biscoff banana bread pudding layers in a jar
The jar from the side, showing the layers
A spoonful of pudding with melted Biscoff on top

recipes.intro: Peak is… upgrading your daily yogurt bowl to this. Layers of Biscoff biscuit, vanilla protein pudding, banana and melted Biscoff, with 20g of protein in one jar.
method: Crush the biscuits. Press some into the bottom of a jar for the base and save the rest for the top.
Spoon in a layer of the protein pudding.
Add a layer of banana slices.
Drizzle over some of the melted Biscoff.
Repeat the layers until everything is used up.
Finish with the rest of the biscuit crumble on top.
recipes.tip: Look at those layers! Build it in a glass jar so you can see them.
recipes.seoTitle: Biscoff Banana Bread Pudding (20g Protein, 4 Ingredients)
recipes.description: Layers of Biscoff biscuit, vanilla protein pudding, banana and melted Biscoff in a jar. 4 ingredients, 5 minutes and 20g protein. Protein Snack Hack episode 4.

recipes.title: Chocolate Peanut Yogurt Bowl
recipes.seoTitle: Snickers Protein Yogurt Bowl (31g Protein, Crackable Chocolate Shell)
recipes.description: The protein dessert that tastes like a Snickers: chocolate peanut Greek yogurt with dates under a crackable dark chocolate shell. 31g protein.
recipes.intro: The protein dessert that tastes like a Snickers! Creamy chocolate peanut yogurt with chopped dates, under a crackable dark chocolate and peanut shell. 31g of protein in one bowl.
method: Mix the PB powder with water into a paste.
Stir in the yogurt and protein powder until creamy.
Fold in the chopped dates and top with the split ones.
Melt the chocolate, stir in the peanuts and spread it over the top.
Freeze for 10 minutes, then crack and dig in.
recipes.tip: Add the PB drizzle for full Snickers vibes!

photos.alt: A Snickers-style chocolate peanut yogurt bowl with a cracked chocolate shell and peanuts

recipes.title: Healthyish Marble Cake
recipes.seoTitle: Healthyish Marble Cake (Almond Flour, Sweetened with Apple Sauce and Honey)
recipes.description: A healthyish chocolate marble loaf cake made with almond flour and sweetened with apple sauce and honey. 7 ingredients, one loaf tin, 6g protein a slice.
recipes.intro: Cake for breakfast? This healthyish marble cake is naturally sweetened with apple sauce and honey and made with almond flour. 7 ingredients and one loaf tin, with an optional hazelnut butter and chocolate orange topping.

groups.name: Batter
items: ¼ cup honey (plus more to taste)

groups.name: Topping (optional)
items: Terry's chocolate orange segments, to decorate

method: Whisk the apple sauce, eggs and honey.
Mix in the almond flour, baking soda and vanilla.
Halve the batter and stir the cocoa into one half.
Layer both into a lined loaf tin and swirl.
Cover with foil and bake for 50 minutes at 170°C.
Let it cool, then add the topping if you like.
recipes.tip: It's not too sweet as it is, so add more honey to taste.
recipes.noteExtra: Cake only, without the optional topping.

recipes.title: Chocolate Pistachio Truffles
recipes.description: No-bake chocolate pistachio truffles: a fudgy date, tahini and cocoa centre dipped in white chocolate and pistachio cream. Makes 20, about 210 kcal each.
recipes.time: No bake, 30 min in the freezer
recipes.intro: The no-bake treat that tastes like a truffle! A fudgy chocolate centre that you'd never guess is made from dates and tahini, dipped in a white chocolate and pistachio coating. 6 ingredients, no oven.
method: Soak the dates in boiling water, then drain.
Blend the dates and tahini, then add the cocoa and salt.
Roll into 20 balls and freeze for 30 minutes.
Melt the white chocolate and stir in the pistachio cream.
Dip each ball, let it drip, then sprinkle with chopped pistachios.
recipes.tip: Use medjool dates for extra sweetness!

photos.alt: A chocolate pistachio truffle broken open to show the fudgy centre
Holding a chocolate pistachio truffle over the batch
A plate of chocolate pistachio truffles

recipes.title: Caramel Almond Crunch Bowl
recipes.seoTitle: Caramel Almond Crunch Bowl (25g Protein, 3 Ingredients)
recipes.description: A 3-ingredient protein breakfast: Greek yogurt with a Pip & Nut caramel almond protein bar turned into crunchy granola and almond butter clusters, plus red grapes. About 25g protein.
recipes.intro: POV: you upgraded your breakfast with only 3 ingredients. Greek yogurt, a Pip & Nut caramel almond protein bar taken apart into crunchy granola and almond butter clusters, and juicy red grapes.

items: 1 Pip & Nut caramel almond protein bar, layers separated
A handful of red grapes, halved

method: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Peel the nut butter top off the base.
Crumble the base over the yogurt.
Halve the grapes and arrange them round the edge.
Microwave the nut butter top for 30 seconds, then roll it into little balls.
Pile the clusters in the middle and dig in.
recipes.tip: Mix it all together for creamy, crunchy, juicy bites!

photos.alt: A spoonful of yogurt with an almond butter cluster over the caramel almond crunch bowl
A spoonful with a halved grape and an almond butter cluster
The three ingredients: a Pip & Nut bar, Greek yogurt and red grapes

recipes.title: Protein Coffee Frappuccino
recipes.description: A thick, frothy protein coffee frappuccino with espresso, vanilla protein powder and almond milk. 25g protein and 150 kcal, with a mocha version.
recipes.intro: Your coffee shop frappuccino, made at home with 25g of protein. Espresso, vanilla protein powder, almond milk and ice, blended until thick and frothy.

groups.name: Optional
items: 1 tsp chia seeds, or a pinch of xanthan gum

method: Add everything to a blender.
Blend until thick and frothy.
recipes.tip: Fancy a mocha? Use chocolate protein powder and chocolate almond milk instead. That makes it about 185 kcal.

photos.alt: A glass of protein coffee frappuccino

recipes.title: Brownie Batter Ninja Creami
recipes.seoTitle: Brownie Batter Ninja Creami (Banana Ice Cream, No Protein Powder)
recipes.description: Tastes like brownie batter: banana and cocoa Ninja Creami ice cream with PBfit and a crumbled chocolate cake mix-in. About 200 kcal and 9g protein a serving.
recipes.intro: Tastes like brownie batter! A banana and cocoa ice cream made in the Ninja Creami, with crumbled chocolate cake spun through. The base is all natural ingredients: no protein powder, no gums and no artificial sweeteners.

items: 150ml SuperNutrio milk, or to the fill line

method: Blend everything, then freeze overnight in the Creami tub.
Spin on the gelato setting.
Add the crumbled cake and spin on the mix-in setting.
recipes.tip: No Creami? Freeze sliced bananas, then blend it all in a food processor until creamy. Any high-protein milk works.

photos.alt: A scoop of brownie batter Ninja Creami ice cream with chunks of chocolate cake

recipes.title: Oreo Cheesecake Ninja Creami
recipes.seoTitle: Oreo Cheesecake Ninja Creami (Cottage Cheese Ice Cream)
recipes.description: High-protein Oreo cheesecake ice cream made in the Ninja Creami with cottage cheese, banana and maple. No protein powder, about 140 kcal and 7g protein a serving.
recipes.intro: Creamy and dreamy, just like Oreo cheesecake. The base is 5 simple ingredients with no protein powder and no artificial sweeteners, just banana and maple.

items: Almond milk, to the max fill line

method: Blend it all, then top up with almond milk to the max fill line.
Freeze overnight in the Creami tub.
Spin on the lite ice cream setting.
Add the crushed Oreos and spin on the mix-in setting.
recipes.tip: No Creami? Blend everything and freeze it in a tub, then add the Oreos and re-blend before serving.

photos.alt: A tub of Oreo cheesecake ice cream with a spoon and Oreos on the side
Scoops of Oreo cheesecake ice cream in two glass bowls with Oreos

recipes.title: Blueberry Protein Froyo
recipes.seoTitle: Blueberry Protein Froyo (18g Protein, No Ice Cream Maker)
recipes.description: Greek yoghurt froyo with frozen blueberries under a crackable white chocolate and almond shell. 18g protein, about 230 kcal, no ice cream maker needed.
recipes.intro: POV: froyo's trending again and you're not paying £10 a tub. Greek yoghurt swirled with frozen blueberries under a white chocolate shell you crack into. Creamy, crunchy, and no ice cream maker needed.
method: Sweeten the yoghurt, if you like.
Swirl in the frozen blueberries.
Melt the buttons and stir in the almonds.
Spread the topping over the yoghurt and freeze for 10+ minutes.
Crack it, mix it up and enjoy!
recipes.tip: The Greek yoghurt gives you 15g of protein to keep you full, and the white chocolate is the treat bit: just 15g. The numbers leave out the optional sweetener.

photos.alt: A pot of blueberry froyo with a white chocolate and almond topping
Blueberry froyo with the white chocolate shell cracked and mixed in
The froyo ingredients: Greek yogurt, frozen blueberries, white chocolate buttons and almonds

recipes.title: Mango Cheesecake Protein Pot
recipes.seoTitle: Mango Cheesecake Protein Pot (13g Protein, Ready in 2 Minutes)
recipes.description: The 13g protein snack that tastes like mango cheesecake: mango cottage cheese, frozen mango and a sprinkle of seeds. 3 ingredients, ready in 2 minutes.
recipes.intro: The 13g protein snack that tastes like mango cheesecake! Three ingredients, ready in 2 minutes.

items: ½ pot All Things mango cottage cheese (120g)

method: Start with half a pot (120g) of the cottage cheese.
Add the frozen mango chunks.
Mix it all together.
Sprinkle the seeds on top and enjoy!
recipes.tip: The cottage cheese brings the protein and live cultures, the frozen mango adds vitamin C and fibre, and the linseed and hemp in the seed mix add omega-3s and crunch.

photos.alt: A pot of mango cottage cheese topped with mango chunks and seeds
The mango cheesecake pot from above, next to the cottage cheese lid

recipes.title: Pre-Run Protein Toast
recipes.seoTitle: Pre-Run Protein Toast with Cottage Cheese, Dates and Honey
recipes.description: The perfect pre- and post-run snack: sourdough with smashed dates, cottage cheese and honey, air fried for 2 minutes. 17g protein and 60g carbs.
recipes.intro: The ultimate pre-run snack: cottage cheese toast. Sourdough and dates fuel your run, cottage cheese keeps you full, and it works just as well after your run. Shout out to Finks Bakery (@finks.london) for the sourdough.
method: Slice the sourdough.
Smash the dates onto the toast.
Spoon over the cottage cheese.
Air fry for 2 minutes at 180°C.
Drizzle with honey and enjoy.
recipes.tip: More time? Soak the dates in boiling water for 3–5 minutes for a jammy texture.

photos.alt: A slice of cottage cheese toast with dates, honey and cinnamon

recipes.title: Chocolate Apple Cups
recipes.seoTitle: Chocolate Apple Cups (No Bake, with a Date "Caramel")
recipes.description: No-bake chocolate apple cups with a soft date and crunchy almond butter centre, topped with seeds. Makes 6, about 280 kcal each.
recipes.time: No bake, 30 min in the fridge
recipes.intro: Apple season is here! Melted dark chocolate cups filled with a soft date, crunchy almond butter and chopped apple, then covered in more chocolate. The "caramel" is just a date.

items: Crunchy almond butter, a dollop each

method: Spoon chocolate into 6 muffin cases.
Add a date and a dollop of almond butter to each.
Pile on the apple, then cover with chocolate.
Sprinkle with seeds and chill for 30 minutes in the fridge.
Peel off the cases and enjoy.

photos.alt: A plate of chocolate apple cups topped with seeds
A chocolate apple cup bitten in half to show the date and almond butter
A chocolate apple cup up close

recipes.title: Viral Apple Salad
recipes.seoTitle: Viral Apple Salad with Date Caramel (14g Protein)
recipes.description: The viral apple salad with a magic date caramel: green apple, Greek yogurt, almond butter and chocolate chips in a jar. About 360 kcal and 14g protein.
recipes.intro: The viral apple salad with a magic date caramel. Crunchy green apple, Greek yogurt, almond butter and chocolate chips in a jar: lid on, shake, stir and dig in.

groups.name: Date caramel
items: 1 date and 10ml tahini per spoonful, blended

method: Blend the dates and tahini into a caramel.
Chop the apple into a jar.
Add the yogurt, almond butter and caramel.
Top with the chocolate chips and cinnamon.
Lid on, shake, stir and dig in.
recipes.tip: Make a big jar for the whole week!

photos.alt: The viral apple salad layered in a jar
A spoonful of apple salad lifted from the jar
A spoon in the apple salad jar

recipes.title: Apple Brownie for One
recipes.description: A fudgy brownie for one made with just 2 ingredients: an air-fried apple and dark chocolate. About 395 kcal.
recipes.intro: A fudgy brownie for one with just 2 ingredients: an apple and dark chocolate. The apple goes in the air fryer, then gets blitzed with melted chocolate until smooth and fudgy.
method: Air fry the apple for 15 minutes at 190°C.
Melt the chocolate and pour it over the apple.
Blitz until smooth and fudgy.
Press into a silicone mould.
Chill for 15 minutes in the fridge, or 5 in the freezer.
Turn it out, top with a walnut and enjoy.
recipes.tip: In a rush? 5 minutes in the freezer!

photos.alt: An apple brownie for one topped with a glazed walnut
A spoonful of fudgy apple brownie
A fudgy apple brownie with a bite taken out

recipes.title: Rice Paper Apple Pie
recipes.seoTitle: Rice Paper Apple Pie (Air Fryer, About 160 kcal)
recipes.description: Crunchy air fryer apple pies made with rice paper: jammy cinnamon apple, maple syrup and walnuts. Makes 2, about 160 kcal each.
recipes.intro: The easiest, lightest apple pie you'll ever eat. Jammy cinnamon apple wrapped in rice paper, brushed with maple syrup and air fried until it's crunchy outside and soft inside.

items: Maple syrup (to cook, brush and drizzle)

method: Cook the apple with maple syrup, cinnamon and cornflour until sticky.
Soften the rice paper and wrap up the filling.
Brush with maple syrup.
Air fry for 12 minutes at 200°C.
Drizzle with maple syrup and top with walnuts.
Serve with Greek yogurt.
recipes.noteExtra: Excludes the yogurt. Add 100g Greek yogurt for +10g protein.

Two rice paper apple pies with maple syrup, walnuts and Greek yogurt
The jammy apple inside a rice paper apple pie
A rice paper apple pie in a bowl with yogurt and walnuts
Two rice paper apple pies and Greek yogurt from above

recipes.title: Apple Crumble Breakfast Oats
recipes.description: Apple crumble for breakfast: warm cinnamon apple, a crunchy almond oat crumble and vanilla protein yogurt layered in a jar. About 320 kcal and 21g protein.
recipes.intro: Apple crumble… for breakfast?! Warm cinnamon apple, a crunchy almond and oat crumble and vanilla protein yogurt, layered in a jar. Like dessert for breakfast.

items: ½ tbsp maple syrup, plus cinnamon

groups.name: To top
items: 1 pot vanilla protein yogurt, or any yogurt plus protein powder

method: Cook the apple with cinnamon until soft.
Toast the oats and almonds, then add the maple syrup.
Stir in the almond flour and yogurt to make clumps.
Layer the apple, crumble and protein yogurt.
Dust with cinnamon, lid on and enjoy.
recipes.tip: Make double the crumble for tomorrow!
recipes.noteExtra: Estimate with a vanilla protein yogurt.

A spoonful of apple crumble breakfast oats
